en.headline: Privacy watchdog starts compliance check on Laguna City face recognition plan
en.dek: The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data is reviewing a proposed facial recognition entry system at the Lam Tin estate after residents raised concerns.
body: The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data has begun a compliance check on a plan by the management company of Laguna City in Lam Tin to install facial recognition gates for resident entry.

The commissioner said facial images are sensitive personal data and the estate has about 8,000 households. The office asked the company for further information to ensure any collection, holding, processing or use of biometric data meets the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance and data protection principles, especially on security.

A staff member of the management company told media the system was meant to give residents more secure entry options. Residents can choose facial recognition or continue using their resident cards and may decline the facial method. The system is not yet in full use.

Private housing estates in Hong Kong rarely deploy facial recognition for routine entry. The commissioner said residents who believe their privacy has been affected can contact the management company or the office.

zh.headline: 私隱署就麗港城人面識別門禁計劃展開循規審查
zh.dek: 個人資料私隱專員公署因藍田麗港城住戶關注，正審查物業管理公司擬引入的人面識別出入系統。
body: 個人資料私隱專員公署已主動對藍田麗港城物業管理公司計劃引入人面識別閘機的安排展開循規審查。
公署指出，面容影像屬敏感個人資料，而麗港城約有8000戶。公署已要求有關機構提供進一步資料，以確保在收集、持有、處理或使用生物辨識資料時，符合《個人資料（私隱）條例》及保障資料原則，特別是資料保安規定。
管業處職員向傳媒表示，系統旨在為住戶提供更多安全出入選擇。住戶可選擇人面識別或繼續使用門卡，亦可拒絕使用人面識別。系統目前尚未全面啟用。
本港私人屋苑較少以人面識別作日常出入管制。公署表示，如住戶認為個人資料私隱受影響，可向管業公司或公署查詢。
